_doc: Character system (드라마 등장인물): the rig's geometry in local units and every staging's shots in screen px. One source of truth for video/src/rig.ts, Body.tsx, Character.tsx, Animal.tsx, CastScene.tsx and tests/test_characters.py, which checks the composition rules: eyes in the eye band, faces and hands never in the caption band / bottom 20% / right UI column (unless a foreground prop hides them), shot sizes, the body-length rule, at most 3 characters per shot. Local rig units: origin at the base of the neck, y down; a character drawn with scale k at (x, eyeY) has its neck at (x, eyeY - rig.eyeY * k).
_characters: ad = the voice of an on-screen ad (watch_ad): drawn as a generic invented presenter inside the TV frame, never a real person
_registry: characters/family/callers are the legacy cast (they also have a human skin). Any story may cast a registry character (content/characters/<id>.json, video/src/registry.ts, radar.production.characters): species = the animal skin's templates (Species.tsx; the hedgehog is reserved for 도치), roleKinds = what the story uses it for (family / caller / other / presenter; rig.ts and script.py read the kind, not the id), outfits and characterProps = the drawn clothes and the one prop that says who it is; a new character's body comes from bodyClasses (height x build).
_expressions: deflated / caught (2026-10-17): the fox's other defeat looks. deflated = ears down, half-closed eyes, a flat mouth, the gloom shade; caught = wide eyes, one sweat drop, the mouth zipped shut. A defeat face shows ONE panic symbol set (sweat / shock lines / gloom), never all of them. defeatFaces = the fox's defeat looks the twist close-up rotates through when the script sets no twist_face (by ep, else a hash of the id: rig.ts defeatFaceOf, script.py twist_face_of).
_castStyles: A skin over the same rig and stagings (script field cast_style, default human): human = Character.tsx, animal = Animal.tsx (진돗개 family: father white, mother tan with a perm; 여우 callers: scammer in a hoodie and headset, fake_banker a silver-grey fox in a suit with a blank badge, ad presenter in a shiny suit). Both skins share the body (Body.tsx, 'bodies'). The animal head keeps to the rig's head box: ear tips no higher than rig.head.top, half width (with cheek fur) within rig.head.rx + 34, the jowl/chin no lower than rig.head.chin; eyes and mouth on rig.eyeY / rig.mouthY.
_animal: eye: the white of an animal eye in local units (height 2*ry = 17% of the head height); shockedMouth: half width of the shocked mouth (2x = 30-40% of faceWidth), with teeth and tongue
_outlinePx: the ink outline in screen px, the same at every shot size: the rig's stroke widths are divided by the character's on-screen scale

rig._hands: hand centres per gesture and side (L = viewer's left, R = viewer's right); a side a gesture leaves free hangs at rest (paw at the hip)

_bodies: SD body per character (local units, half widths; head height H = 382, head width 320): sh shoulders, w the torso's widest, waistY/waistW the waist, hemY the top's hem, hip, crotch, sole (the feet's bottom), legX/legW the legs' centre and half width, skirt (bottom y, half width). Chin->waist 0.6-0.75 H, torso 1.05-1.2 x the head width, parents ~2.7 heads tall, the children ~2.9, the fox callers ~3.0 (lankier = more threatening).
_bodyClasses: the body of a registry character without a legacy pin (registry.ts bodyOfSpec): height elder ~2.7 heads (sole 616), adult ~2.9 (693), tall ~3.0 (731) with the same waist / hem / crotch lines as the legacy bodies, build slim / regular / broad = the widths; an outfit with a skirt adds skirt [crotch + 138, min(190, hip + 12)]. The same SD rules as 'bodies' (tests/test_character_registry.py).
_shotSizes: head height (hair line to chin) as a share of the 1920 frame height, per shot size. The body-length rule (tests): without visible feet, the body below the chin down to bodyRule.line (or a foreground prop's top) is at most bodyRule.maxBelowChin heads; a 'full' shot shows the feet above that line instead.
_props: foreground props drawn in front of the characters (Sets.tsx ForegroundProp): table = the home's table edge (living room, sofa corner), desk = the office desk (work), ccDesk = the call centre's desk, counter = the side-dish shop's counter (the table of a shop scene). top = the prop's top edge in screen px; it hides the body and the resting paws below it. The front face carries a floor gradient (darker toward the bottom) and, when the edge sits above smallPropMaxTop (the caption band's top), one small prop on the surface at the left edge (a cup, a phone stand or a stack of mail by the kind), so a bust shot's lower 40% is a room, not a flat card; nothing is drawn inside the caption band.
_shots: Per staging, the shots it cuts between. A character entry: who (victim | caller | other | presenter), x (neck x), eyeY, k (scale), turn (-1..1, face turned to the viewer's left/right), gestures used in that shot (for the hand checks; the performance may vary it among those listed in gestures), view (front | back). size: the shot size (shotSizes); prop: the foreground prop; windows: framed insets in screen px.

pip_call._hook: the opening shot (the poster and thumbnail): the victim's extreme close-up with the phone at the ear; the caller's window springs in on the first cut

split_call._split: the caller's panel is the top part (y 236 to the border), the victim's the bottom (border to 1250); the border is tilted 3 degrees

over_shoulder_chat._over: back view: the eye line stands for the back of the head (no face); the phone glows in the hand and the mockup panel floats above it

twist_closeup._stamp: drama packaging: the stamp's look follows the length of the twist text (visible characters, ! and ? count half): a round seal for 1-2 (뚝!), a box for 3-5 (작전 실패, 들켰다), a slimmer box for 6-8 (사기였습니다); centred at x, lifted so its bottom stays above `bottom` (the caption band)

_aside: the inner-voice aside (role inner, 속마음): the speaking character alone, facing the camera in a close-up, the room dimmed around it; who = caller for the callers' rigs (call centre, ccDesk), the family rigs stand in the home behind the table (familyProp)
_packaging: drama packaging over every staging: the disclosure chip (top-left) and the fixed situation title (centred, 1-2 lines of <= 12 characters); content that must stay readable (caller window, floating thread, keyword bubbles) starts below safeTop. spike = where 도치 the 가시 감지기 pops in (feet line, from the left edge; outside the caption band, the bottom 20% and the right column)
_series: series = the chip above the title box (script series + ep): centred, its bottom overlapping the box's top border by `overlap` (a tab on the box), clear of the disclosure chip at the left; it is up for the opening showFrames (the poster and the first beat) and again in the poster tail, so no more than two chips (the disclosure chip and the speaker chip) are on screen during the dialogue (speakerChip.maxChips). speakerChip = the dialogue speaker chip over the captions (dialogue.tsx): its top and text size (>= 26 px; it must read on a 390 px phone). ending = the 도치 stamp ending (2026-10-17, instead of the white end card): in the story's last `frames` (>= minFrames, after a twist stamp + afterStamp, never in the poster tail) 도치 pops up from behind the desk edge at the spike slot (x, feetY, size; clipped at clipY, so it never enters the caption band) over `rise` frames, swings its paw for `swing` frames and a red stamp `text` (the twist stamp's style) lands at stampAt on the chest zone (stamp), next to 도치 (stampAlt = the same spot: the survival stamp is the family's, so it never lands on a face or on the villain's chest); everything fades over the last outFrames. No sound (the last line may still be speaking). rewind = the 'label' chip under the title box for `frames` after a cold open. cold = the flash-forward: the twist frame `settle` frames after the stamp, a slow punch-in to `punch`, an 8-frame rewind wipe (`shrink` = the frame shrinking under it)
_costumes: the fox's disguise per scam (script cast 'costume', caller characters scammer / fake_banker / ad; animal skin only, the human skin keeps the usual look). hoodie = the call-centre hoodie and headset (the scammer's usual look); bank_suit = navy suit, tie, blank lanyard, glasses, a cheap black bowl wig both ears poke through (torn holes) and a crooked fake moustache (whiskers poke out); investigator = dark trench coat with the collar up, a plain brimmed hat the ears poke through, a plain folder (no police uniform, badge or agency mark); courier = a blank cap squashing the ears out sideways, a work vest with grey reflective bands, a parcel; guru = a shiny suit, a slick wig one ear pokes through, a pointer; lecturer = blazer over a turtleneck, round glasses, a thin cheek mic, a closed laptop, the tail tip peeking over the shoulder; family_mask = the hoodie with a cardboard mask of the son's face on a stick held in front of the face, a small card with no ears of its own, so the fox's pointed ears stand whole above it and his cheek fur sticks out round it even in the call window (it slips aside when he is shocked). Every disguise leaks: the gag is that he is always recognisably the fox. Leaks sit at face / forehead / collar height, the part every shot shows (the aside and the twist close-up crop below the title box).
_villainSets: where the caller is (script / scene 'villain_set', default callcentre): the room behind every caller shot (the call window, caller / solo / over-shoulder caller shots, the aside, the twist close-up on a caller and so the cold open), drawn in a 1080x1920 design anchored at the top (the call window and the split panel show its upper part). Identifying things sit in the side strips (x < 200, x > 880) and around the ears, the only background a close-up of the fox leaves. prop = its foreground prop (replaces ccDesk at the same top edge, plain surfaces only), rim = the caller's rim light there, light = the set's key light on his jaw and chest (the call centre's monitor teal). fake_office = a bland office: blinds, a logo-less '상담실' plate, a filing cabinet; studio = a fake finance studio: a chart screen, light panels; car = inside a parked car at night: pillars, street bokeh, the mirror, the dashboard; lecture_room = a small seminar stage: a slide screen (no text), a roll-up banner, a spotlight, the lectern.
_homeSets: the family's room in a drama scene (script set): living = the living room (window, lamp), shop = the side-dish shop (반찬가게: shelves of side-dish tubs, a fridge, a handwritten sign; the home's table becomes the shop counter)
_posterProps: evidence props for the hook frame (script scene poster_prop), taped on the wall beside the character of a solo shot: the box in screen px (x, y = top-left before the small rotation); the character moves to charX so its face stays clear of the prop. mail_notice = a generic '우편물 도착 안내서' (no agency name or mark, masked number and name, an undecodable code square)
_motion: cheap motion, all pure functions of the frame: a punch-in on the scene's keyword (the line's bubble, else the scene's mark when a line says it), a camera shake as a shocked/panicked line starts, a 4-frame squash when a face changes
